source.title: Intrinsic dimension of data representations in deep neural networks
source.authors: Alessio Ansuini; A. Laio; J. Macke; D. Zoccolan

record.tranche_reason: The study trains a network on randomly shuffled MNIST labels and reports its training error, bearing on whether it can fit random labels. It measures representation intrinsic dimension rather than reproducing the original studies’ broader generalization and optimization comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper states that training on shuffled MNIST labels produced zero training error. Its statement that test performance must be at chance is attributed to cited work, not reported as this study’s result. The ID-profile result is recorded separately because it is a measured outcome for the randomly labeled network.
record.test_reason: Section 3.5 reports this study's own zero training error after training a CNN on shuffled MNIST labels. Random-label training and training error match the original method and measure; the separate intrinsic-dimension analysis does not determine the tranche.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the random-label conclusion: the shuffled-label network attains zero training error but shows substantial late-layer intrinsic-dimension expansion, contrasting with late-layer reduction on generalizable data.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a small MNIST convolutional network on fully shuffled labels and reports training error and ID profiles. It does not reproduce the original studies’ broader fit, chance-test-error and optimization-time measurements; Appendix A.1.2 reports different training hyperparameters for MNIST† and original MNIST.
record.method_sensitivity: The MNIST† training setup differs from the original MNIST setup in epochs, learning rate and momentum.

fits_no_version.finding: After training on shuffled MNIST labels, intrinsic dimension grows substantially in later layers and approaches the output embedding-dimension bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label memorization can produce late-layer dimensional expansion rather than the dimensional reduction observed with generalizable data.

record.problems: The random-label result is on one small MNIST convolutional network. The paper does not report test error for that run, and its random-label and original-label training settings differ. The ID result is shown in Fig. 6B, while the text describes its trend without reporting numerical values.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error is attributed to prior work rather than measured for this run. Fitting with unchanged training hyperparameters is not tested; the architecture is unchanged.
Relative time to convergence and convergence as a function of label-corruption fraction are not measured. Training budgets alone do not establish convergence times.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs is not tested. The luminance perturbation retains structured images.
Intermediate label-corruption fractions and their training/test-error trajectories are not tested.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization are not tested.
The temporal order of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels is not measured. Intrinsic-dimension dynamics on clean CIFAR-10 do not establish this order.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's limits_scope verdict with supports for the measured fitting component. Different training settings and an unreported test error leave components untested; they do not establish a failure or necessary qualification.

versions.untested_parts: Test error at chance is not reported as this study’s own result; the paper does not test fitting random labels without changing training hyperparameters.
The study tests only fully shuffled labels, not intermediate corruption fractions or a smooth train/test error trajectory.
The study does not measure whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: small convolutional network for the experiments on the MNIST dataset
rows.operation_detail: Trained the same network on MNIST†, with randomly shuffled labels.

conditions.value: MNIST† (MNIST images with randomly shuffled labels)

rows.note: The paper says the same network as in section 3.4 was used, but Appendix A.1.2 lists different epoch, learning-rate and momentum settings for MNIST† than for original MNIST.
rows.check: Zero training error is correctly recorded. The unchanged-hyperparameter component is untested: original MNIST used 200 epochs, learning rate 0.0004 and zero momentum; shuffled MNIST used 500 epochs, learning rate 0.0005 and momentum 0.9. These choices do not demonstrate that changing hyperparameters was necessary.

rows.subject: small convolutional network for the experiments on the MNIST dataset
rows.operation_detail: Measured the intrinsic-dimension profile across network layers after training on shuffled MNIST labels.

conditions.value: MNIST† (MNIST images with randomly shuffled labels)

rows.baseline: Original MNIST profile is described as the comparison; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.value: It grew considerably in the second half of the network, almost saturating the upper bound set by the embedding dimension in the output layer.
rows.note: This is a representation-geometry finding, not a measure of the label-fitting or generalization behavior specified by the claim versions.
rows.check: The intrinsic-dimension finding is correctly described, but it cannot establish any claim version's behavioral effect. Its observed state should not be interpreted as observing random-label fitting.
